title: Field Elevator & Micro‑Experiment Toolkit — draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact field enablement + micro‑experiment toolkit to run quick, evidence-driven sales conversations with platform and infra engineers. It combines two things: (1) a one‑page elevator test for engineers to validate a value thread in 90 seconds, and (2) a set of ‘microbattle’ A/B experiments sellers can run during pilots to gather measurable signals (latency, cost, error modes, integration friction).

TL;DR (one paragraph):
Sellers and SEs should use a 90s elevator script and three short micro‑experiments during the first pilot week: (A) Latency-to-Value demo (p95 token latency with/without prefix cache), (B) Cost delta test (baseline model vs quantized variant on same workload), (C) Fallback resilience check (model variant + region switch). Each test should take <60 minutes to validate, produce 2–3 datapoints, and feed back into the pilot decision checklist.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Field teams are losing technical credibility when they rely on long engineering conversations without observable evidence.
- Platform engineers care about predictable SLOs and deterministic economics — not marketing slides.
- Many pilots stall because sellers can’t show short, reproducible tests that map to customer SLOs and unit cost.

Audience and when to use:
- Primary: Sales Engineers and Platform Sellers during pilot kickoff and week 0–1.
- Secondary: Solutions engineers and customer success during onboarding.
- Use case: quick qualification, early pilot validation, or rescue when customers say “we need data.”

90s Engineer Elevator (script + checklist):
- Goal: get buy‑in and permission to run microtests.
- Script (90s):
  1) Intro (10s): “Hi — I’m Nina from Redwood, we help teams get predictable LLM inference costs and p95 latency across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.”
  2) Constraint framing (20s): “Most platform teams we meet have two blockers: unpredictable token cost and tail latency spikes. You probably have an SLO like ‘p95 < X ms’ and a budget limit per inference. Is that roughly right?”
  3) Quick evidence ask (20s): “If we could show you three short tests in your environment that prove we can meet p95 and reduce per‑token cost by Y%, would you let us run them on a small dataset?”
  4) Permission + next step (40s): “Great — we’ll run a 60‑minute microtest suite focusing on (1) p95 latency with your typical length distribution, (2) delta cost between model/quantization profiles, and (3) a fallback failover test. I’ll loop in an SE and we’ll ship results and an ops checklist within 24 hours.”
- Quick checklist to hand to the engineer:
  * Confirm a small test endpoint or API key (scoped)
  * Provide 30–100 representative inputs (short list or csv)
  * Identify the SLO to test (p50/p95 target, throughput target)
  * Nominate contact for infra routing/firewall questions

Micro‑Experiments (3 short, reproducible tests):
- A: Latency‑to‑Value (p95 profile)
  * Objective: measure p50/p95 with current config vs Redwood with prefix/KV cache on same sample set
  * Steps (30–45 min): run 200 request sample in parallel at low concurrency, record p50/p95, token counts, and memory spikes
  * Output: CSV with latency percentiles, short narrative, 2‑line replay script for SRE
  * Success signal: p95 reduction >= 10% or stable p95 with lower variance
- B: Cost‑Delta Quickbench
  * Objective: show per‑token cost reduction when switching to a quantized variant or batching profile without >5% quality regression on a small eval set
  * Steps: run same prompts against baseline and quantized model, compute tokens, compute cost using customer pricing envelope or Redwood hosted cost model
  * Output: cost delta, sample mispredictions (3 examples), recommendation (batch/quantize/cache)
  * Success signal: >= 15% cost reduction with acceptable quality delta (team defined)
- C: Fallback & Regional Resilience Shakeout
  * Objective: demonstrate graceful fallback when primary model/region is unavailable and measure failover latency
  * Steps: simulate model variant outage (route to cheaper variant) and region switch, record time-to-first-token and error rates
  * Output: short incident playbook with rollback steps and observed failover metrics
  * Success signal: <500ms additional latency and <1% error increase for accepted fallbacks

Microbattle Card Template (one page, printable):
- Title: [Test name] | Owner: [SE] | Duration: [mins] | Inputs: [#] | Success metric: []
- Why run: 1–2 sentences linking to customer SLOs
- Steps (1–6 numbered, copyable)
- Raw outputs to capture (CSV/links)
- Suggested follow-up action (A/B rollout, model pin, alert)

Sample objection scripts & quick counters (for sellers):
- “We don’t want vendor code in our environment” -> “We’ll use a scoped test key and provide a replay script you can run locally; results are reproducible and we’ll hand you a trimmed runbook.”
- “We need long-term SLAs, not demos” -> “This microtest is explicitly to validate your SLO and budget assumptions; if outcomes look good we fast‑track a Dedicated capacity convo with SLA options.”
- “Quality looks worse on quantized models” -> “We’ll surface 3 representative failure cases from your prompt set and recommend a hybrid fallback: quantized for bulk requests and full‑precision for high‑risk routes.”

Measurement & short report format (one page deliverable per microtest):
- Header: test name, owner, start/end time, environment identifier
- 3 bullet takeaway lines (observed p95, cost delta, risk note)
- CSV links: latency.csv, tokens.csv, errors.csv
- Recommended action (A/B): e.g., enable prefix cache + 2% batching, and schedule a canary on Dedicated lanes

Pilot decision checklist (use within 48h after microtests):
- [ ] p95 within target under sample load
- [ ] per‑token unit cost improvement meets threshold
- [ ] no critical failures in fallback test
- [ ] SRE/infra signoff on routing and keys
- [ ] customer identifies follow-up owner for full pilot

Ops handoff snippet (for CSM/Onboarding):
- Deliverables to hand off: one‑page microtest report, replay scripts, a small canary config (route + model pin), and an alert playbook for fallback behavior.
- Recommended canary: 1% traffic for 48–72h with metrics collection (p95, errors, cost).

Experiment A/B matrix (quick):
- Variant A: Baseline model + default batching
- Variant B: Quantized model + prefix cache + conservative batching
- Success axis: cost vs p95 vs filetered quality regressions
- How to run: parallel traffic split or sequential runs with identical inputs and traffic shaping

Playbook checklist for SE prior to running tests:
1) Get explicit written permission and scope (API key, test endpoint)
2) Confirm sample set and SLOs in a quick Slack thread + attach csv
3) Prepare replay script and small infra notes (ports, regions)
4) Run tests and capture outputs in designated folder with timestamps
5) Produce one-page report and choose next action: canary, revisit, or stop

Appendix: quick templates (copy/paste)
- Slack ask template: "Hi @eng, can we run a 60m microtest against scoped test endpoint to validate p95 and cost for 200 sample requests? We'll provide scripts and results; please confirm API key and sample csv."
- Replay run (bash): curl loops with json payloads and simple jq timing to capture latencies (example included in attached github PR)

Open questions & next iterations (for this draft):
- Add a small cheat sheet for procurement objections (T&Cs and data residency asks)
- Create printable microbattle card PDF for in-person field events
- Record two short screencasts for the SE kit (latency demo and cost table walkthrough)

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to align cost math with pricing table from Product (ask Priya for the latest per-token calculation)
- Samir to add a quick Terraform snippet for spinning a scoped test endpoint in Private deployments

End of draft.
